Oscar-Winning star Eva Marie Saint’s cause of death disclosed The cause of death of Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint has been revealed. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 10:30 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 10:30 IST

Eva Marie Saint (Image source: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The cause of death of Oscar-winning actress Eva Marie Saint has been revealed. As per a death certificate obtained by PEOPLE, the actress died following the onset of cardiopulmonary arrest. Eva breathed her last on October 6. She is survived by her husband of more than six decades, television director Jeffrey Hayden, their two children, Darrell and Laurette, four grandchildren and two great-grandchildren.Born on July 4, 1924, in Newark, New Jersey, Saint studied at Bowling Green State University in Ohio. She began her career in television and radio before making her Broadway debut in The Trip to Bountiful in 1953, according to PEOPLE magazine. As per the publication, Saint made her film debut in 1954 with Elia Kazan’s ‘On the Waterfront.’ Her performance as Edie Doyle earned her the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. She was just two days away from giving birth to her first child when she received the Oscar. While accepting the award, Saint joked, “I may have the baby right here!” She went on to appear in several films, including That Certain Feeling, A Hatful of Rain, Raintree County, Exodus, All Fall Down, 36 Hours, Grand Prix, The Russians Are Coming, The Stalking Moon and Cancel My Reservation. However, one of her most remembered roles came in Alfred Hitchcock’s 1959 thriller North by Northwest. Saint played Eve Kendall opposite Cary Grant in the film, which became one of the most popular movies of her career.Saint also had a long career on television and continued working across different formats over the years. She married Jeffrey Hayden in 1951 after the two met on a subway. Hayden directed several popular television shows, including Leave It to Beaver and The Incredible Hulk. The couple later appeared together in a San Francisco production of A.R. Gurney’s Love Letters in 2011. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Student protests erupt across Indonesia over rising living costs, forest fires Student protests erupted across Indonesia over rising living costs, economic concerns and forest fires, with demonstrators criticising President Prabowo Subianto's policies on the second anniversary of his administration, The Jakarta Post reported. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 09:40 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 09:40 IST

Demonstrators protest against the government's handling of wildfires and demand an end to corruption, collusion and nepotism, in Jakarta (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Student protests erupted across Indonesia over rising living costs, economic concerns and forest fires, with demonstrators criticising President Prabowo Subianto's policies on the second anniversary of his administration, The Jakarta Post reported. Demonstrations took place in Jakarta, Yogyakarta and Bandung in West Java on Tuesday, as students and civil society groups voiced concerns over economic pressures, environmental damage and civil liberties. In Jakarta, hundreds of university students gathered around the Tugu Tani monument, demanding action on rising living costs and the government's handling of forest and peatland fires. The fires have generated toxic haze, disrupted flights, forced school closures and raised public health concerns. Protesters called on the government to declare the prolonged forest fires a national disaster, prosecute companies responsible for environmental damage, tackle corruption and make education and healthcare more affordable. They also demanded stronger protection for freedom of expression. According to RT, protesters in Indonesia also set a police truck on fire amid the unrest. Indonesia has struggled to contain forest fires in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Papua amid an unusually severe El Niño-driven dry season. The resulting haze has spread to neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia, prompting concerns over regional air quality and public health, The Jakarta Post reported. Amid the protests, Presidential Chief of Staff General Police Listyo Sigit Prabowo said President Prabowo Subianto chaired a limited meeting at Merdeka Palace in Jakarta on Monday to discuss accelerating efforts to tackle forest and land fires. In a post on X, Listyo said the President had instructed authorities to strengthen aerial operations and improve coordination among the Indonesian National Armed Forces, National Police, National Disaster Management Agency, local governments and communities. The President also called for investigations into 98 corporate cases suspected of being linked to forest and land fires to be expedited, Listyo said, adding that the Presidential Chief of Staff's office would oversee the government's response and ensure law enforcement proceedings were based on evidence and conducted in accordance with applicable regulations. Separately, Greenpeace Indonesia activists climbed the Welcome Monument at Jakarta's Hotel Indonesia traffic circle on Tuesday and unfurled large banners protesting what they described as the government's failure to address persistent wildfires, The Jakarta Post reported. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
"I want it to work out": Prince Harry says he wants to "reconcile" with King Charles, Prince William According to PEOPLE, the Duke of Sussex spoke about his relationship with his father and elder brother in a new interview with GQ magazine. During the conversation with GQ’s Zach Baron, Harry admitted that the family situation was something he continued to grieve. ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 09:36 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 09:36 IST

Prince Harry (Source: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Prince Harry recently shared that he wants to resolve his family rift with King Charles and Prince William, saying that reconciliation is the most important thing amid everything happening in the world. According to PEOPLE, the Duke of Sussex spoke about his relationship with his father and elder brother in a new interview with GQ magazine. During the conversation with GQ’s Zach Baron, Harry admitted that the family situation was something he continued to grieve. When asked about his “complicated relationship” with his father and brother, Harry acknowledged that family disputes were something many people could relate to. He also spoke about his wish to repair the strained relationships. “That continues to come up with me the whole time by people that I speak to. So I know how relatable it is,” Harry said, as per PEOPLE. He added that he understood why people were interested in his family situation and hoped his experience could help others dealing with similar problems. “And some people don’t want it to work out. I want it to work out,” he added. Following the interview, a spokesperson for Harry clarified that his comment about some people not wanting things to work out was not directed at Prince William or any other member of the royal family. Harry further spoke about the importance of making peace with family members, saying that he wanted to move past the differences. “With everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile. That’s the key point,” he said. When asked whether the family rift could be repaired, Harry replied, “Yeah, of course.” He also spoke about how people could deal with painful experiences from the past. While acknowledging that emotional scars could remain, he encouraged people to change their outlook and try to move forward. “Look, scars stick around forever, but what your perception is and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, certainly letting go of the past, that’s something that I would encourage everybody to do,” he said. Harry added that family disputes should not continue to take up space in people’s lives when there was already enough trouble in the world. According to PEOPLE magazine, Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, stepped back from their roles as working members of the British royal family in 2020. Their decision brought greater public attention to the family’s strained relationships. The couple later spoke about their experiences in their 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey, their 2022 Netflix docuseries and Harry’s 2023 memoir. King Charles and Harry reunited over the summer. The meeting also marked Charles’ first time seeing Meghan and the couple’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, in four years. However, Harry and William have reportedly not been in direct contact. Royal author Russell Myers recently told PEOPLE that William’s position on his relationship with his younger brother remained unchanged. According to Myers, William believes his father’s relationship with Harry and the Sussex family is a matter for Charles to decide. He added that William does not see himself having a relationship with the Sussexes, either privately or in an official capacity, in the future. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
"Hormuz is closed until America accepts our conditions": Araghchi demands US to honour MoU commitments "What we want from the American side is adherence to all the commitments contained in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding that was signed earlier," Araghchi said. "After they adhere to these commitments, we can enter into negotiations on other cases." ANI | Updated: 21-10-2026 09:35 IST | Created: 21-10-2026 09:35 IST

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has declared that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed to maritime traffic until the United States accepts Tehran's terms and fulfils its existing diplomatic commitments. Speaking in an interview with Iraq's Al-Ikhbariya network, relayed by state broadcaster IRIB, Araghchi emphasised that Washington must first adhere to the terms of the previously signed Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding before any broader negotiations can take place. "Our position on the Strait of Hormuz is clear and unambiguous; we have previously announced and emphasised it," Araghchi stated. "The American side must accept our conditions to open the strait to ships and vessels. Before such an understanding or agreement is reached, the strait will naturally be closed, and the movement of ships and vessels through the strait and existing routes will face problems." Araghchi made it clear that Tehran will not enter into fresh negotiations on other issues until Washington honours its earlier promises. "What we want from the American side is adherence to all the commitments contained in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding that was signed earlier," Araghchi said. "After they adhere to these commitments, we can enter into negotiations on other cases." Addressing ongoing diplomatic channels, Araghchi revealed that indirect communications with Washington are continuing through regional intermediaries, including Pakistan and Qatar. He referenced a proposal previously submitted by Iran known as the "Seven-Day Plan". "Our negotiations with the American side through intermediary countries, including Pakistan and Qatar, are continuing continuously," he noted. "We previously presented an initiative to the American side called the Seven-Day Plan, in which we clearly stated our conditions." According to Araghchi, the proposal outlined a timeline for reopening the vital waterway. "The Strait of Hormuz was supposed to be fully opened on the sixth day of this period," he said, adding that while Washington signaled agreement, it sought to introduce additional clauses on topics already addressed in prior talks. Araghchi noted that "in the final stage of negotiations, any issue or problem raised by either party can be discussed and a final agreement can be reached". Rejecting American economic and military pressure, Araghchi affirmed that Washington's efforts to isolate Iran or force its surrender through coercion or regional pressure will fail. "We have entered a deep quagmire, and therefore we are witnessing military threats, the imposition of economic sanctions, and the imposition of new sanctions," Araghchi said. He added that US attempts to pressure neighbouring states against cooperating with Iran have not received a positive response. "The American side should know that these measures will not work," Araghchi warned. "Iran will not surrender in any way, neither to economic sanctions nor to military threats. The only appropriate solution is diplomacy and a negotiated solution." Clarifying Iran's position on the legal framework governing the waterway, Araghchi underscored that the Strait of Hormuz lies entirely within territorial waters. "The Strait of Hormuz is located in the internal waters of Iran and Oman and has no connection with international waters," Araghchi stated. "If the Strait of Hormuz were to open one day, the route that Iran and Oman have agreed upon would be the actual and agreed-upon route for ships to pass through; not another route." He added that Iran and Oman have already reached an agreement regarding shipping lanes in the strait and are currently awaiting its international registration. Araghchi's remarks come amid continuing tensions between Tehran and Washington, with both sides exchanging accusations over the conflict and the prospects for diplomatic engagement. (ANI)
